subject: Request: temporary retention variance and backup handoff for EU sandbox
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary retention variance and backup handoff for EU sandbox

Hi Jonas,

We're preparing to run a time-sensitive data migration for our EU sandbox next week and need a short, formal variance to the standard backup purge cadence. Specifically:

- Request: hold last nightly backups for the sandbox project (project id: acme-eu-sbx) for an additional 30 days beyond the default 14-day retention to allow for a staged restore and vendor validation.
- Rationale: third-party validation of migration results requires access to point-in-time backups and a delayed purge window to capture logs and telemetry for the validator.
- Evidence needed: a signed amendment to the DPA or a short-term retention waiver; confirmation of which subprocessors will have access during the extended window; export path for audit logs.

I've attached our retention_request_form.docx and a proposed timeline. Can Redwood provide:
1) a short DPA amendment draft we can sign, or
2) confirmation that Redwood can apply a one-off backup hold for the EU sandbox and provide an audit log export endpoint?

We are on a tight timeline — planning to begin the migration on 2026-09-05. Please let us know the internal owners and estimated turnaround.

Thanks,
Emma Rivera
Ops Manager, Acme Health
ops@acmehealth.com

Attachment: retention_request_form.docx (docx)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and timeline.

Quick status: I'm looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (ops) to land on the exact amendment language and the operational steps for a temporary hold.

Kimberly / Karthik — can you review the attached form and confirm:
- whether we can implement a 30-day hold on nightly backups for the sandbox (acme-eu-sbx) starting 2026-09-05, and what the operational steps are to ensure the copies are not purged accidentally;
- whether we need any changes to the DPA (short amendment vs documented waiver) or a signature from Acme Legal;
- which subprocessors will have access during the hold and whether an HSM/KMS key rotation impacts restore ability.

Emma — cc'ing Mina from infra in case there are infra-side constraints we should know about. We'll aim to get a proposed amendment and an operational plan by end of day Monday 2026-08-31.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Product Lead, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: backup-schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary retention variance and backup handoff for EU sandbox

Thanks Jonas — quick read-through from Legal. High level: we can do a short-term variance but prefer a signed DPA amendment (1 page) that:

- Explicitly limits the variance to project acme-eu-sbx and a defined 30-day window starting 2026-09-05.
- States that backups held under the variance are for validation only and will be immutable until the end of the window.
- Confirms which subprocessors will be able to access the held backups (we must list each subprocessor by name and purpose).
- Includes a clause requiring Acme to notify Redwood of any external validator access (if external validators require credentials, we need names/emails).

Operational notes:
- Subprocessors: CloudWorks (storage), LogShip Inc. (log aggregation) will be the only subprocessors used for this. We should have a short attestation from CloudWorks that they will not perform additional processing beyond storage and restore assistance.
- KMS: If Acme wants a dedicated key for the held backups, we can offer customer-managed KMS for the sandbox (requires 48–72 hrs to provision and test). Otherwise, note that regular key rotation timelines may make some point-in-time restores more complex; we must lock the relevant key policy for the variance period.
- Logs: we'll provide an export (compressed) of audit logs for the hold period. Format will be newline-delimited JSON, S3-compatible endpoint (details in proposed ops plan).

I've drafted suggested amendment language and attached DPA_amendment_v2.pdf — please review and edit. If Acme signs, Ops can trigger the hold.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: DPA_amendment_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary retention variance and backup handoff for EU sandbox

Folks — operational plan and roll-up:

1) Acceptance criteria: signed amendment (DPA_amendment_v2.pdf) from Acme Legal.
2) Provisioning: if Acme opts for customer-managed KMS, we need 72 hrs to provision and validate. If not, we'll lock Redwood's key policy for the acme-eu-sbx snapshots for the 30-day window.
3) Hold procedure: we will set a backup 'hold' tag on the nightly snapshots (internal flag prevents automated purge). The snapshots will be moved to an immutable retention class for the duration.
4) Access controls: only Redwood SREs on the incident response roster and the listed CloudWorks/LogShip service accounts will have restore permissions. We will require a pull request with a justification ticket for any manual restore.
5) Audit artifacts: we will provide an audit bundle (snapshot manifest + NDJSON access logs + checksums) to Acme via the S3 endpoint: s3://redwood-acme-eu-sbx/holds/2026-09-05-2026-10-05/audit-bundle.tar.gz. Access link will be time-limited and logged.
6) Timeline:
   - 2026-08-31 EOD: Redwood sends final amendment for signature.
   - 2026-09-02: provision KMS if requested.
   - 2026-09-05: apply hold to nightly snapshot pipeline.
   - 2026-10-05: expiry of variance; begin normal purge workflow unless Acme requests extension with a new signed amendment.

Open questions for Acme: which account(s) will the external validator use? If they require RBAC access, we need names/emails to set up read-only credentials. Also confirming that CloudWorks will provide the attestation Kimberly mentioned — I've cc'd their contact in prior thread (subproc@cloudworks.com) but we need written confirmation.

If Legal is happy, I can turn this into an internal runbook and pre-flight checklist.

- Karthik (for Infra Ops)
